issues.detail: Covers mostly the happy path with only brief notes on errors (exitOverride, invalid choices) and omits handling of unknown commands/options, async action rejections beyond parseAsync, and a missing-argument error example.

scenarios.name: mandatory-choice-option
scenarios.rationale: Both use new Option with .choices, .makeOptionMandatory, .addOption and state the error lists allowed choices and exits with code 1, but B has a more realistic setup (a deploy subcommand, program.parse()) and adds correct, useful extra cases such as the missing-option error, exitOverride and the Commander version requirement.

scenarios.name: variadic-lint-with-parser
scenarios.rationale: Both declare `<folders...>` and `--max-warnings <count>` with a parser and default 0, and show the action getting `folders` as an array and `opts.maxWarnings` in camelCase; B adds a validating parser and more edge-case detail, while A's plain parseInt matches the rubric's example more directly.

scenarios.name: async-cli-packaging
scenarios.rationale: Both cover parseAsync, the bin mapping to dist/cli.js, type module and the shebang; A is more thorough with a full tsconfig and extra notes, while B is concise and covers the same rubric items, but its inclusion of top-level await and a vague commander version note adds nothing the rubric needs.
